correctness.rationale: Deleting the common vertex leaves m copies of P5; deleting its closed neighborhood leaves m copies of P3. The resulting joins are homotopy spheres of dimensions 2m−1 and m−1. The P5 complex collapses to the oriented four-cycle 1,4,2,5,1, which path reversal inverts; reversal of P3 preserves both components. The link inclusion is nullhomotopic by connectivity, giving the ordinary wedge. The integral exact sequence identifies the lower homology naturally with the suspended link and the upper naturally with the deletion because m≥2 separates the dimensions. Swapping join factors of dimensions d,e contributes (−1)^((d+1)(e+1)), yielding the two integral signs. The common vertex is uniquely of degree 2m, so all automorphisms are as stated. Both characters are nontrivial, making the rational quotient acyclic by rational averaging on an admissible subdivision. Independent finite replay counted 194, 2322, 29186 faces including empty and matched all 8, 48, 384 signed Lefschetz values for m=2,3,4 respectively; it is corroboration, not the integral or all-m proof.
residual_risks: Neither an equivariant wedge splitting nor integral homology of the quotient is established or claimed.
